body:
I can reproduce this on 4.5.beta3 on Linux + NVIDIA, although it looks different:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29720e2e-1681-43c4-88b7-f3f860c9f32e

However, you can resolve the issue by increasing the subdivision on the ground mesh (`MeshInstance3D` in the MRP). Set **Subdivide Width** and **Subdivide Depth** to `1` on the PlaneMesh resource:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e9ba8d4-a1d6-457c-9d2e-a1857a6ee620

Doing so may resolve the issue on AMD too. If the issue persists to a certain extent, try higher subdivision values like `3`, `7`, `15` or `31`.

This is a similar issue to shadow pancaking where it'll break with huge unsubdivided meshes. The issue you're encountering here is different though, but it also affects texture UV mapping if you affect a texture to the PlaneMesh. This is mentioned in its class reference:

> **Note:** When using a large textured **PlaneMesh** (e.g. as a floor), you may stumble upon UV jittering issues depending on the camera angle. To solve this, increase `subdivide_depth` and `subdivide_width` until you no longer notice UV jittering.

Note that https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100896 doesn't resolve this issue (I just tried it), regardless of the camera Z far value you use in the editor.

This is a simple floating point precision issue with figuring out where the pixel needs to sample the shadow map, due to too massive triangles.
This will vary slightly depending on GPU architecture even within the same brand.

This same issue will also be visible with just a Normal Texture.

It'll also show most at the edges of the triangles (of which the plane is made of 2 by default, and those two will mismatch)

I see. Increasing the subdivisions of the plane did the trick. Thanks to everyone for your help.
